assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature priority is 'Major' (feature-standard.md line 6). summary-comment.md documents: 'Priority: Major -- propagated to all tasks. The Feature's priority is "Major" (not "Undefined"), so it is included in the additional_fields of each created task as "priority": {"name": "Major"}.' The additional_fields JSON block confirms '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature has Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (feature-standard.md line 7). No fixVersion scope setting in CLAUDE.md (absent, defaults to 'both'). summary-comment.md documents: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated to all tasks. The Feature has a non-empty fixVersions array containing "RHTPA 1.5.0". No fixVersion scope setting exists in Jira Field Defaults (absent), so the default scope "both" applies, meaning fixVersions are propagated to tasks. Each created task includes "fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}] in its additional_fields.'
